newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN CALL MONEY ENDS UP, GILTS STEADY TO DOWN.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN CALL MONEY ENDS UP, GILTS STEADY TO DOWN.

text.p: Indian two-day money ended Thursday at 5.5-6.5 percent, up from opening quotes of 1.0-3.0 percent on tighter funds supply, dealers said.
They said some big lenders were absent from the market and this reduced the availability of funds in the market, pushing rates up.
"Trade was a bit volatile today," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Most of the morning's deals were between 1.0 percent and 4.0 percent but rates rose to 5.0-6.0 percent in the afternoon."
Dealers said rates went up to 7.0-8.0 percent in stray deals just before the close.
Call money is likely to open around 7.0-8.0 percent on Saturday, they said.
Dealers said government securities were steady to down in moderate trade as high call money rates depressed sentiment.
"Many market players were surprised at the rates today," said a dealer at a private bank. "If call money remains at this level, prices of government securities will fall."
The 12.59 percent 2004 bond traded at 107.18 before ending at Wednesday's close of 107.
The 11.83 percent 2003 inched up to 103.68 from 103.65.
The 11.19 percent 2005 ended at 100.48 against 100.47 while the 10.85 percent 2001 was unchanged at 100.68.
